statement: Live, HANSEI is behind holding by 5.1% after 34 sessions.

statement: Live, its worst fall so far is -1.4% against holding's -2.6%.

statement: In 6 replayed crises its worst fall was clearly smaller than holding's in 4, and it finished ahead of holding in 1.

Replays use real prices and the real brain, with the news advisor silent.

statement: PPO earns a higher Sharpe than buy-and-hold across walk-forward folds.
evidence: PPO trailed holding by -0.44 Sharpe (95% CI -0.70 to -0.17) and was ahead in 11% of folds. This is why HANSEI is a simple, explainable agent.
source: Before the Lab: A deep-RL policy (PPO) against holding

statement: Each advisor's liked-minus-disliked return spread is positive, 20 sessions ahead.
evidence: 6 of 6 spreads have a 95% interval that includes zero. No advisor is a statistically reliable return signal; the volatility brake predicts bigger swings, not lower returns.
source: Before the Lab: Do the advisors predict returns?

statement: A more-invested rule keeps most of the drawdown protection and earns more.
evidence: On 2020 onward it beat holding by +1.22% a year against the live rule's +1.03%, with a lower Sharpe edge (+0.15 vs +0.23). A later check on the falling Jul 2024 onward window had it behind the live rule. Not switched on.
source: Before the Lab: Staying more invested (tolerance 0.2, floor 0.5)

statement: With news, HANSEI earns more than without it over Jul 2024 onward.
evidence: News added +0.44% a year, with a 65% chance of being better than no news: noise. On its own the news view was right 46% of the time over 1,733 opinions. It stays live because it is cheap and its live record is short.
source: Before the Lab: Does reading the news help?

statement: Adding it raises returns against the four-advisor rule in tune and holdout.
evidence: It lowered 2007-2019 returns by -0.32% a year and helped in 5 of 9 holdout settings. Small cross-sectional edges do not survive a hold-by-default design. Not added.
source: Before the Lab: An earnings-surprise advisor

statement: It falls less than holding and has a higher Sharpe, in both spans. It is not expected to earn more.
evidence: Met its own criteria but not the reviewer's: beats noise. Met 4 of 4 criteria written before the run.
source: Lab experiment: The live rule against holding

statement: It beats holding while the five-stock basket is in a downtrend and lags while it is in an uptrend, in both spans.
evidence: Did not meet what it promised before the run: ahead in downtrends, 2007-2019; ahead in downtrends, 2020 on; behind in uptrends, 2007-2019; behind in uptrends, 2020 on. Met 0 of 4 criteria written before the run.
source: Lab experiment: Where the edge comes from

statement: Silencing trend makes HANSEI worse: a lower Sharpe than the live rule in both spans.
evidence: Did not meet what it promised before the run: worse without it, 2007-2019. Met 1 of 2 criteria written before the run.

statement: Learning helps: with it switched off, Sharpe is lower than the live rule in both spans.

statement: It holds by default and never borrows.
evidence: In replays the engine was up to 109% invested: cash dips below zero when holdings outgrow their slots. The live paper book cannot do this, so replays are slightly more aggressive than live.

statement: A trade is worth making only when wanted and held exposure differ by a third of a slot.
evidence: The Sharpe edge over holding was positive in 9 of 9 nearby settings on 2020 to 2026. That shows the result is not one lucky setting, not that this setting is best.

statement: A view should be judged 20 sessions later, against a liquid fund.
evidence: A design choice. No experiment has compared it with other horizons.

statement: Trust should move slowly (learning rate 0.05).
evidence: Chosen because faster rates traded more in backtests. Whether learning helps at all is a separate, open question in the Lab.

statement: ₹10,000 in five equal slots, bought in whole shares, represents the strategy fairly.
evidence: Live it has wanted 62% invested on average and held 46%; 23 queued orders filled nothing. One share of the dearest stock is most of a slot. The replays trade rupee amounts and do not have this drag.

statement: ICICI Bank moves about 14.8% with a 10% move in the market.
evidence: Sensitivity +1.48, 95% interval +1.38 to +1.61, from 943 weekly returns (2007-09-24 to 2026-11-12). Before 2017: +1.62; after: +1.23. The later years fall OUTSIDE what the earlier years alone predicted, so it has shifted.

statement: With Fixed-Share, Sharpe is higher than with plain Hedge in both spans.
evidence: Invalid run. A variable-name collision in the replay engine meant the Fixed-Share setting never reached the learner and the baseline was corrupted with it, so the variant came out identical to the baseline to the last digit. The bug was found the same day; the reviewer now fails any variant that is identical to its baseline. Superseded by 'fixed-share-corrected'.
source: Lab experiment: Fixed-Share in place of plain Hedge
